outcomeNote: Mishna stating the law with a tannaitic dispute over the basket case.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ טוֹמְנִין בְּשִׁלְחִין וּמְטַלְטְלִין אוֹתָן, בְּגִיזֵּי צֶמֶר וְאֵין מְטַלְטְלִין אוֹתָן. כֵּיצַד הוּא עוֹשֶׂה? נוֹטֵל אֶת הַכִּסּוּי, וְהֵן נוֹפְלוֹת.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» «One may insulate» cooked food on Shabbat eve «in» animal «hides and may move» those hides on Shabbat. So too, one may insulate food «in wool fleece and,» in contrast to hides, «one may not move» the fleece. «How,» then, «does one act» if he insulated food in fleece, and now wishes to remove the pot? «He lifts the cover,» which he is permitted to move, «and» the fleece «falls» by itself. He need not even touch it.

segments.he: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אוֹמֵר: קוּפָּה, מַטָּהּ עַל צִדָּהּ וְנוֹטֵל, שֶׁמָּא יִטּוֹל וְאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְהַחֲזִיר. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: נוֹטֵל וּמַחֲזִיר.
segments.en: «Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:» If he placed the pot in «a basket» filled with fleece, «he leans» the basket «on its side» so that the fleece will fall to the side «and takes» the pot. Otherwise, there is concern «lest» the wool collapse when «he lifts» the pot from the basket. «And» then, «he will be unable to replace» the pot, as it is prohibited to move the wool to make room for the pot, since the wool is set-aside. «And the Rabbis» disagree and «say: He may take» the pot «and» afterward «replace it.»

moves.summary: one may insulate in hides and move them, in fleece without moving it; lift the cover and the fleece falls
a basket is tilted on its side so the pot can be taken without the fleece collapsing

moves.summary: the Rabbis permit taking and replacing
